title: A damaged sofa delivery
prompt: You ordered a sofa from an online furniture store. It arrived last week with a deep tear in the fabric, and the delivery driver would not take it back. You have called the store twice without a clear answer. Write an email to the store’s customer relations department in about 150 to 200 words.
points: Describe the damage and what happened at delivery
Explain what you have already done to solve the problem
Say whether you want a replacement or a refund, and by when

title: Heating repair request
prompt: The heating in your apartment has been working poorly for two weeks, and nights are now close to freezing. You mentioned it once to the building superintendent, but nothing has been done. Write an email to your landlord in about 150 to 200 words.
points: Describe the problem and how long it has lasted
Explain how it is affecting your daily life
Ask for a repair date and suggest a time when you will be home

title: Covering a shift
prompt: You have been invited to a family event out of town next Saturday, but you are scheduled to work that day at the café where you work part-time. You would like a coworker to take your shift. Write an email to a coworker you get along with but do not know very well in about 150 to 200 words.
points: Explain why you need the day off
Offer something in return, such as covering a future shift
Say how and when they can let you know

title: Housewarming invitation
prompt: You have just moved into a new apartment and want to celebrate with your friends. Write an email to a group of close friends in about 150 to 200 words.
points: Give the date, time and place of the party
Tell them what food and drinks there will be and what they could bring
Explain how to get to your new place by transit or car

title: Thank you to a mentor
prompt: A senior colleague spent several months guiding you through a difficult project at work. The project finished successfully last week, and you are about to move to a different team. Write an email to your mentor in about 150 to 200 words.
points: Thank them and describe one specific way they helped
Explain what you learned from the experience
Suggest keeping in touch, for example over coffee

title: Registering a child at school
prompt: Your family is moving to a new neighbourhood in Calgary next month, and you want to register your ten-year-old child at the local elementary school. The school’s website has little information. Write an email to the school’s office administrator in about 150 to 200 words.
points: Introduce yourself and explain your situation
Ask which documents you need and what the registration deadline is
Ask about before-school and after-school care

title: Missed garbage collection
prompt: The city has not collected the garbage or recycling on your street for two weeks in a row. Bags are piling up outside several homes, and your neighbours are starting to complain. Write an email to the city’s waste services department in about 150 to 200 words.
points: Describe the problem and when it began
Explain why it is a concern for residents
Ask when collection will resume and how the missed pickups will be made up

title: A cabin weekend
prompt: You and five friends have been talking about a weekend away. You have found a cabin near a lake that could work, but it costs more than you expected and you need everyone’s agreement soon. Write an email to your friends in about 150 to 200 words.
points: Describe the cabin, the dates and the total price
Suggest how to share the costs and the driving
Ask everyone to reply with their availability by a specific day

title: Saying no to a party
prompt: A friend has invited you to a big birthday party on a weekend when you must prepare for an important exam. You really want to go but cannot. Write an email to your friend in about 150 to 200 words.
points: Thank them for the invitation and show you care about the event
Explain honestly why you cannot attend
Suggest another time to celebrate together

title: Feedback on a course
prompt: You have just finished a ten-week English communication course at a community college. Overall it was useful, but there were some problems, such as unclear assignments and a very crowded classroom. Write an email to the program director in about 150 to 200 words.
points: Say what you liked most about the course
Describe two things that could be improved
Suggest specific changes for future students

title: Meeting your new neighbour
prompt: A new family has moved into the apartment next to yours. You have only said hello in the hallway, and you would like to start a friendly relationship. Write an email to your new neighbour in about 150 to 200 words.
points: Introduce yourself and welcome them to the building
Share some useful information about the area or the building
Invite them to a short get-together or offer your help

title: Downtown pool or park
prompt: Your city has received a one-time grant of $5 million and is asking residents how to spend it. Choose the option you prefer and explain your reasons in about 150 to 200 words.
options: Option A: Build a new indoor community pool and fitness centre
Option B: Redesign the central park with new trails, gardens and a stage

title: Four-day work week
prompt: Your company is testing a new schedule and has asked employees for their views. Choose the option you prefer and explain your reasons in about 150 to 200 words.
options: Option A: A four-day week with ten-hour days and every Friday off
Option B: A five-day week with flexible start and finish times each day

title: College work placements
prompt: Your college is revising its business diploma and is asking students for input. Choose the option you prefer and explain your reasons in about 150 to 200 words.
options: Option A: Make a four-month paid work placement mandatory for every student
Option B: Keep placements optional and add more elective courses instead

title: Summer street festival
prompt: Your neighbourhood association has funds for one big event this summer and wants to hear from residents. Choose the option you prefer and explain your reasons in about 150 to 200 words.
options: Option A: A weekend street festival with live music and food trucks
Option B: A weekly farmers’ market with local crafts and small family activities

title: Bike lanes or parking
prompt: Your city is redesigning a busy main street and is asking residents for their opinions. Choose the option you prefer and explain your reasons in about 150 to 200 words.
options: Option A: Replace street parking with protected bike lanes
Option B: Keep street parking and build a new parking garage nearby

title: Where to live
prompt: A housing agency is asking newcomers to your city where they would prefer to live. Choose the option you prefer and explain your reasons in about 150 to 200 words.
options: Option A: Rent a small apartment close to downtown, work and transit
Option B: Rent a larger house in the suburbs with a longer commute

title: Self-checkout tills
prompt: A large grocery store chain is deciding how to organize its stores and has sent customers a survey. Choose the option you prefer and explain your reasons in about 150 to 200 words.
options: Option A: Replace most cashiers with self-checkout machines to keep prices lower
Option B: Keep staffed checkouts and offer self-checkout only as an extra choice

title: Workplace wellness
prompt: Your employer will start a wellness benefit and wants to know which one staff would value more. Choose the option you prefer and explain your reasons in about 150 to 200 words.
options: Option A: A yearly allowance for gym memberships and sports equipment
Option B: Three extra paid days per year for mental health and rest

title: Charity choice
prompt: Your office raises money together each year and is voting on where the donation should go. Choose the option you prefer and explain your reasons in about 150 to 200 words.
options: Option A: A local food bank that supports families in your city
Option B: An international organization that provides clean water to villages

title: Holiday style
prompt: A travel agency is asking customers how they prefer to take a week-long holiday. Choose the option you prefer and explain your reasons in about 150 to 200 words.
options: Option A: An all-inclusive resort where meals and activities are organized
Option B: An independent trip where you plan your own routes and stay in small guesthouses

title: Neighbourhood improvement
prompt: Your local council has a small budget to improve your neighbourhood and is asking residents to choose. Choose the option you prefer and explain your reasons in about 150 to 200 words.
options: Option A: Install brighter street lighting and more security cameras
Option B: Create a community garden and a new playground in the empty lot
